title: GenAI at the Edge: Comprehensive Survey on Empowering Edge Devices
extended_summary:
This paper is a comprehensive survey of research on deploying generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) models on edge devices. It addresses the problem that modern GenAI systems, including large language models and diffusion models, are typically too computationally and memory intensive for resource-constrained edge hardware, while cloud-only deployment raises latency, privacy, and connectivity concerns.

The paper does not study an educational intervention or any teacher- or student-facing program. Instead, it organizes the technical literature into three broad categories: software optimization, hardware optimization, and deployment frameworks. Within software optimization, it reviews model compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation, along with neural architecture search and open-source model adaptation. Within hardware optimization, it surveys accelerator designs and attention-optimization methods for LLMs and diffusion models. It also reviews systems and frameworks such as TensorRT, TVM, EdgeMoE, CoreInfer, and super-resolution acceleration pipelines.

Because this is a survey rather than an empirical study, it does not report a participant population, controlled comparison, subgroup analyses, or outcome effects. Its main conclusion is that progress in co-design across algorithms, hardware, and frameworks is making GenAI increasingly feasible on edge devices, but important challenges remain around personalization, security, latency, and energy efficiency.

identified_tools.description: Generative AI systems based on large language models and foundation models that generate new data or content such as text and images.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a survey of GenAI techniques for deployment on edge devices; it does not evaluate an instructional coaching or lesson feedback product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a survey paper on edge deployment of generative AI, not an empirical study of an educational intervention. It does not report controlled, quasi-controlled, or subgroup analyses relevant to teacher coaching or feedback.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational outcomes or impact estimates are reported. The paper provides background and synthesis on system optimization only, so there is no measured instructional impact to rate.
